title: Pre-existing failure, or a regression from this branch
description: One noul over two verify log tails. It judges provenance only, once both states are already in hand.
actsNote: Nothing acts on an answer from this set. Nothing-acting is the safety mechanism, not shadow mode. See docs/adrs/0008-no-question-set-acts-in-this-campaign.md.

scope.statement: THE EXPENSIVE HALF OF THIS PROBLEM IS NOT THE JUDGEMENT. It is acquiring the baseline state — checking out the default branch, booting it, and running the gates again — and that wants a caching verb rather than a classifier. This set judges only once BOTH states are already in hand. A run that has only the branch's own failure has nothing for this set to answer and must acquire the baseline first.
scope.note: A classifier asked to guess the baseline it was never given would be answering a different, easier question and scoring well on it.

carries: the verify log tail from this branch
the verify log tail from the same gate on the default branch
the changed-file list for the branch
state.note: Both tails are required. Conversation-derived state leaving the device is gated twice, off by default, and printable with --dry-run.

eval.statement: THIS SET CARRIES NO EVAL NUMBERS. Do not look for one elsewhere; none exists. The screenshot keep is bounded at 7 days, so the corpus is a few dozen runs on one device; and verdict.json records red/green for a RUN, not the provenance of a specific failure, so even the surviving runs do not contain the label.

questions.noul: This failure is a regression introduced by the branch under test, rather than a failure that is already present on the default branch.
questions.answerMeans: 1.0 means the branch introduced it; 0.0 means it was already failing on the default branch before this branch existed.
questions.why: The same failure text can be produced by a branch's own change or by a gate that was already red, and telling them apart is a comparison between two log tails rather than a property of either one.
